title: Admin Runbook Playground: author, simulate, and export runbooks-as-tasks
creator: Aisha Cohen
description: Build an interactive 'Runbook Playground' (web UI + small CLI) that lets SREs and support engineers author runbooks as composable tasks, simulate their execution against synthetic incidents, and export validated task graphs to the Ops Playbook Runner. Goal is to reduce time-to-author for runbooks, catch obvious failures locally, and standardize telemetry/instrumentation for every step.
background: We currently maintain many runbooks as markdown docs and ad-hoc scripts. Converting them to orchestrated tasks is manual and error-prone. This playground will accelerate runbook-onboarding, provide fast feedback loops, and produce runnable artifacts with metadata (retries, timeouts, required secrets). It aligns with the long-term runbook-as-code initiative.
acceptance_criteria: Web UI prototype where engineers can create a 5-step task flow with step types: shell, HTTP, runbook-call, and pause
Simulation harness that can inject a synthetic alert payload and execute the task flow in dry-run mode without touching production resources
Export function that emits a validated task graph (YAML) compatible with Ops Playbook Runner v1.6
Automatic generation of telemetry hooks for each step (trace/span names, metrics tags) that appear in the Console's ops-playbook dashboard
SRE review completed and security checklist passed (secrets handling, least-privilege execution patterns)
implementation_steps: Design: simple flow-editor canvas (nodes + edges) and step property panel
Backend: lightweight task schema service with validation API (schema stored in config repo)
Simulator: containerized sandbox environment that can stub outbound calls and emulate common failure modes
Exporter: YAML generator with schema versioning and a small linter
Instrumentation: inject OpenTelemetry spans and counters for each step; wire to existing ops-console ingest
Auth: integrate with existing admin service account token exchange and KMS for secret placeholders
E2E: run sample conversion of 3 canonical runbooks (Database failover, Helix agent restart, Cache flush)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Simulator might accidentally run destructive commands in non-sandboxed envs -> Mitigation: strict sandboxing + dry-run mode default
Risk: Secrets exfiltration when exporting runbooks -> Mitigation: placeholders only; require explicit secret-binding step that references KMS; disallow plain-text secrets
Risk: Exported YAML incompatible with older runner versions -> Mitigation: version tag in export and compatibility checks in linter
notes_and_progress: 2026-01-18 - Aisha Cohen: Kicked off discovery with two SREs and 3 support engineers; collected 7 example runbooks. Consensus: need simulator and step templates for common ops patterns.
2026-01-22 - Marco Lin: Completed initial data model for task schema; pushed to config repo branch 'playground/schema-v1'. Waiting on review from infra-models team.
2026-01-26 - Priya Nanduri (SRE): Reviewed simulator plan. Requested ability to stub AWS RDS calls and create a non-destructive 'read-only' emulator for database steps.

2026-01-30 - Marco Lin: Prototype backend PR opened (see links). Unit tests added for schema validation. Notes: need to add stricter sandbox containment; failing CI on one test that executes /bin/rm in containerized harness.

2026-02-02 - Design review: UX feedback from Elina Park. Suggested inline step templates and quick-import from existing markdown runbooks. Action: add import transformer task to scope. Next: schedule security review for Feb 4.
qa_plan: Create 10 synthetic incidents spanning common failure classes (network, auth, load, disk full)
Run each exported task graph in simulator and verify expected telemetry and non-destructive behavior
Automated regression test that lints exports and runs simulator smoke test in CI
Security QA: secret handling verification and threat model review
rollout_and_metrics: Rollout: internal alpha to SRE/support teams (week 1), beta to 3 oncall rotations (week 3), GA when export/use increases and no major issues by week 8

Success metrics: time-to-author metric down by 40% for converted runbooks; simulator adoption by 80% of runbook authors within 2 months; <1 incident caused by exported runbook in first quarter after GA
Monitoring: track exports per week, simulator dry-run failures, and number of linter errors per export
review_feedback: Elina Park (Design): prefer collapsible advanced settings per step; avoid overwhelming users with too many options by default
Priya Nanduri (SRE): require explicit non-production mode toggle and 'safe-mode' default
Security: require approval flow for exported runbooks that reference privileged secrets
final_notes: This ticket is the orchestration 'spike' + MVP build for runbook playground. Follow-ups will include tighter runner integration, RBAC controls for export, and telemetry QA. Maintain minimal surface area on first release to reduce blast radius.
